# Study design

## Clinical question

**Among adults with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or ulcerative
colitis who newly initiate a JAK inhibitor, does receiving the recombinant
zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) within 3 months of JAK inhibitor initiation
reduce incident herpes zoster over 2 years, compared with no vaccination
during that window?**

## Why this question requires CCW

JAK inhibitors substantially increase herpes zoster risk. Clinical guidelines
recommend RZV prior to or at the time of JAK inhibitor initiation, but
real-world vaccination rates are low and timing is variable. A naive
comparison of vaccinated vs. unvaccinated JAK inhibitor users is vulnerable
to two problems.

**Immortal time bias.** A patient who receives RZV on day 60 has survived 60
days without herpes zoster before entering the "vaccinated" group. Assigning
all their follow-up to the vaccinated group credits the vaccine with 60 days
of event-free time it did not cause.

**Confounding by indication.** Patients who receive RZV tend to be older,
more engaged with preventive care, and treated by more proactive providers —
all of which independently predict herpes zoster risk. Standard baseline
covariate adjustment cannot correct for confounding that evolves over the
follow-up window.

CCW addresses both problems. Every patient is cloned into both arms
simultaneously at cohort entry, so baseline balance is guaranteed. A clone
is censored only when its observed behavior deviates from its assigned
protocol. Inverse probability of censoring weighting corrects for the
informative nature of that censoring.

## Target trial

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Eligibility | Adults with RA, PsA, or UC; new JAK inhibitor user (none in prior 365 days); no prior RZV in past 5 years; ≥ 365 days prior observation |
| Arm 1 | Receive first dose of RZV within 90 days of JAK inhibitor start |
| Arm 2 | No RZV within the first 90 days (vaccination after day 90 is permitted) |
| Assignment | Cloning at JAK inhibitor start date |
| Follow-up | Until herpes zoster, death, disenrollment, or 730 days |
| Outcome | Incident herpes zoster |
| Causal contrast | Per-protocol effect of early vaccination vs. deferred or no vaccination |

---

# Cloning mechanics: a minimal example

Before specifying the full analysis, it helps to see exactly what cloning
does to a small, hand-crafted cohort.  The five subjects below cover every
scenario that arises with a 90-day grace period.

```{r toy-data}
library(dplyr)

toy_cohorts <- data.frame(
  subjectId       = 1:5,
  cohortStartDate = as.Date("2020-01-01"),
  cohortEndDate   = as.Date("2021-01-01"),   # 366 days (leap year)
  initiationDate  = as.Date(c(
    "2020-02-15",  # Subject 1 — vaccinated on day  45 (within grace period)
    "2020-05-01",  # Subject 2 — vaccinated on day 121 (after grace period)
    NA,            # Subject 3 — never vaccinated
    "2020-03-01",  # Subject 4 — vaccinated on day  60; herpes zoster at day 213
    NA             # Subject 5 — never vaccinated; herpes zoster at day 152
  ))
)

toy_outcomes <- data.frame(
  subjectId   = c(4L, 5L),
  outcomeDate = as.Date(c("2020-08-01", "2020-06-01")),
  outcomeId   = c(1L, 1L)
)

toy <- createCloneCensorWeightData(toy_cohorts, toy_outcomes)
```

The raw cohort table shows when (if ever) each subject initiated treatment —
the only piece of information the cloning algorithm requires.

```{r toy-cohort-table}
dplyr::collect(toy$cohorts) |>
  mutate(
    initiationDay = as.integer(initiationDate - cohortStartDate),
    outcomeDay    = c(NA, NA, NA, 213L, 152L)
  ) |>
  select(subjectId, initiationDay, outcomeDay) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Subject", "Vaccination day", "Outcome day"),
    caption   = "NA = never vaccinated / no outcome"
  )
```

Now define the two arms and run the cloning step.

```{r toy-arms}
arm_initiate <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "rzv_within90",
  strategyType = "initiateWithin",
  gracePeriod  = 90,
  label        = "RZV within 90 days"
)

arm_defer <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "no_rzv_within90",
  strategyType = "deferBeyond",
  gracePeriod  = 90,
  label        = "No RZV within 90 days"
)
```

```{r toy-clone}
cloned <- createClonesAndCensor(
  toy,
  arms         = list(arm_initiate, arm_defer),
  gracePeriod  = 90,
  washoutPeriod = 0
)
```

```{r toy-clone-table}
dplyr::collect(cloned$cohorts) |>
  select(subjectId, arm, survivalTime, artificiallyCensored, event) |>
  arrange(subjectId, arm) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Subject", "Arm", "Survival days", "Artificially censored", "Event"),
    caption   = paste(
      "Each subject appears twice — once per arm.",
      "survivalTime is the number of days the clone is under observation.",
      "artificiallyCensored = 1 when the clone's observed behaviour",
      "deviated from its assigned protocol."
    )
  )
```

Reading across the table clarifies several key properties of CCW:

- **Guaranteed balance at baseline.** Every subject enters both arms on the
  same date with the same prior history; there is no baseline confounding by
  construction.

- **Complementary censoring.** Subjects 2, 3, and 5 follow the `no_rzv_within90`
  protocol and are censored from arm `rzv_within90` at day 90. Subjects 1 and 4
  follow the `rzv_within90` protocol and are censored from arm `no_rzv_within90`
  at their initiation day.  After day 90 every subject's observed behavior is
  consistent with exactly one arm.

- **Outcome credit goes to the arm that earned it.** Subject 4 received RZV on
  day 60 and developed herpes zoster on day 213. That outcome appears only in the
  `rzv_within90` arm — the `no_rzv_within90` clone was already censored at
  day 60.  The mirror image holds for Subject 5: because they never vaccinated,
  their outcome on day 152 accrues entirely to the `no_rzv_within90` arm.

- **IPCW corrects for informative censoring.** The artificial censoring above is
  not random: subjects who are healthy and well-managed are more likely to receive
  RZV promptly, so the subjects who *survive* in the `rzv_within90` arm are a
  selected group.  The inverse probability of censoring weights estimated in the
  next phase reweight each arm back to the uncensored target population.

# Creating the analysis settings

Every analytical choice in a CCW study is captured in a hierarchy of R6
settings objects. This design allows specifications to be validated at
construction time, serialized to JSON, and shared or reproduced across
sites and Strategus pipelines before any data are touched.

## Treatment strategy arms

`createArmDefinition()` specifies the protocol a clone in each arm is
assigned to follow. The `strategyType` determines the censoring rule applied
when observed data deviate from the protocol:

- `"initiateWithin"` — censored if treatment has **not** occurred by day
  `gracePeriod`.
- `"deferBeyond"` — censored if treatment occurs **within** day
  `gracePeriod`; initiation after that window is consistent with the
  strategy.

Together these form a grace period comparison: once the 90-day window
closes, every patient's observed behavior is consistent with exactly one arm.

```{r arms}
armVaccinate <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "rzv_within90",
  strategyType = "initiateWithin",
  gracePeriod  = 90,
  label        = "RZV within 90 days of JAK inhibitor start"
)

armDeferred <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "no_rzv_within90",
  strategyType = "deferBeyond",
  gracePeriod  = 90,
  label        = "No RZV within 90 days"
)
```

## Data extraction

```{r db-args}
# Exclude RZV concept IDs so the treatment does not appear as a predictor
# in the IPCW models.
rzvConceptIds <- c(1160056L, 1160057L)

dbArgs <- createGetDbCloneCensorWeightDataArgs(
  washoutPeriod     = 365,
  covariateSettings = FeatureExtraction::createDefaultCovariateSettings(
    excludedCovariateConceptIds = rzvConceptIds,
    addDescendantsToExclude     = TRUE
  )
)
```

## Study population

```{r pop-args}
studyPopArgs <- createCreateStudyPopulationArgs(
  removeSubjectsWithPriorOutcome = TRUE,
  priorOutcomeLookback           = 365,
  minDaysAtRisk                  = 1,
  riskWindowEnd                  = 730,
  endAnchor                      = "cohort start"
)
```

## Cloning and censoring

```{r clones-args}
clonesArgs <- createCreateClonesAndCensorArgs(
  arms           = list(armVaccinate, armDeferred),
  intervalLength = 30
)
```

## IPCW weights

```{r weights-args}
weightsArgs <- createCreateCensoringWeightsArgs(
  trim      = c(0.01, 0.99),
  maxWeight = 10
)
```

## Outcome model

```{r outcome-args}
outcomeModelArgs <- createFitOutcomeModelArgs(
  modelType         = "cox",
  varianceEstimator = "robust"
)
```

## Full analysis specification

`createCcwAnalysis()` assembles all step-level objects into a single,
validated, serializable specification.

```{r analysis}
analysis <- createCcwAnalysis(
  analysisId                     = "main_90day",
  description                    = "Primary: RZV within 90 days vs. deferred",
  getDbCloneCensorWeightDataArgs = dbArgs,
  createStudyPopulationArgs      = studyPopArgs,
  createClonesAndCensorArgs      = clonesArgs,
  createCensoringWeightsArgs     = weightsArgs,
  fitOutcomeModelArgs            = outcomeModelArgs
)
```

## Target cohort and outcomes

`createTargetArmOutcome()` links the analysis to specific cohort definition
IDs in the database. Negative control outcomes are included alongside the
primary outcome to support empirical calibration.

```{r tao}
#  101      New JAK inhibitor users with RA, PsA, or UC
#  102      First dose of RZV — used for both arms; strategyType determines
#           how each arm interprets initiation events
#  201      Incident herpes zoster (primary outcome)
#  301-320  Negative control outcomes for empirical calibration

tao <- createTargetArmOutcome(
  targetId                    = 101L,
  arm1CohortId                = 102L,
  arm2CohortId                = 102L,
  outcomeIds                  = c(201L, 301:320),
  excludedCovariateConceptIds = rzvConceptIds
)
```

## Top-level specifications

`createCcwAnalysesSpecifications()` combines all analyses and target-arm-outcome
definitions into the object accepted by `runCcwAnalyses()`.

```{r specs}
specs <- createCcwAnalysesSpecifications(
  ccwAnalysisList      = list(analysis),
  targetArmOutcomeList = list(tao)
)
```

---

# Saving and sharing the specification

The full specification can be written to JSON and shared across sites or
checked into version control. `loadCcwAnalysisList()` reconstructs all R6
objects from the file, including nested arm definitions.

```{r save-load}
analysisFile <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
taoFile      <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")

saveCcwAnalysisList(list(analysis), analysisFile)
saveTargetArmOutcomeList(list(tao), taoFile)

reloaded <- loadCcwAnalysisList(analysisFile)

reloaded[[1]]$analysisId
reloaded[[1]]$createClonesAndCensorArgs$arms[[1]]$armId
reloaded[[1]]$createClonesAndCensorArgs$arms[[1]]$gracePeriod
reloaded[[1]]$fitOutcomeModelArgs$varianceEstimator
```

```{r show-json}
cat(readLines(analysisFile), sep = "\n")
```
